title: pinning-entitlement-and-onramp-scenarios-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft to align product/ops/legal on how pinning entitlements should be represented in contracts and how we operationalize customer onramps. Focus is on: entitlement matrix (what customers can ask for), concrete onboarding scenarios (greenfield vs migration), runtime enforcement signals, and a minimal operator checklist for rollout.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem connectors) and Dedicated where customers require region/territory guarantees.
- Not a legal contract; this is an ops + product primer to inform contract language and SOWs.
- We assume customers will either request: (A) soft pin (preferred region, fallback allowed), (B) hard pin (no cross-region host), or (C) salted pin (data stored in primary region but compute allowed in approved secondary region).

Definitions (quick):
- Pin: customer-asserted binding that a tenant's data or inference must originate and remain in a target region or set of regions.
- Hard pin: requests must be routed only to nodes physically in pinned region(s). Fail closed or enter degraded mode if capacity unavailable.
- Soft pin: attempt preferred region, but requests may be routed elsewhere if capacity or latency SLOs require; must log evidence and surface to customer.
- Entitlement: contractual flag + metadata (regions, tolerance for fallback, audit retention window).

Entitlement matrix (proposal):
- Contract field names we should expose: pin_level, pin_regions, fallback_policy, audit_window_days, migration_window_days, escalation_contact.
- pin_level values: HARD | SOFT | NONE.
- fallback_policy values: FAIL_CLOSED | ALLOW_FALLBACK_WITH_NOTICE | ALLOW_FALLBACK_SILENT.

Example rows (to use in SOW templates):
1) Enterprise EU-only (HARD): pin_level=HARD, pin_regions=[eu-west-1], fallback_policy=FAIL_CLOSED, audit_window_days=365, migration_window_days=90
2) Startup APAC-primary (SOFT): pin_level=SOFT, pin_regions=[ap-northeast-1,ap-southeast-1], fallback_policy=ALLOW_FALLBACK_WITH_NOTICE, audit_window_days=90, migration_window_days=30

Onramp scenarios and operations playbook (high level):
A. Greenfield customer that demands HARD pin
  - Pre-reqs: capacity reserved in target region (dedicated pool or Private infra), signed SOW specifying FAIL_CLOSED, acceptance criteria for latency and throughput.
  - Steps: create tenant with pin metadata; provision region-only routing rule; run residency acceptance tests (see AAT checklist below); schedule a smoke test with customer; enable audit logging to retention specified.
  - Operator notes: if capacity pressure occurs, oncall receives automatic runbook with options: (1) request supplemental capacity, (2) notify customer and throttle, (3) activate backup tenant in-region if pre-provisioned.

B. Migration from hosted API to Private with soft pin requested
  - Pre-reqs: migration window and grace period defined in contract, migration runbook, data-transfer plan.
  - Steps: mirror customer tenant into target region, begin phased cutover by traffic sampling (10% -> 50% -> 100%), monitor pin-violation-rate and error budget. If violations exceed thresholds, rollback to previous routing policy.
  - Key metrics: route_fallback_rate, request_latency_p50/p95, KV-cache-warmup-time.

C. Emergency fallback when hard pin cannot be satisfied (rare)
  - If hard pin physical capacity is exhausted and customer contract includes disaster SLA that allows prioritized cross-region temporarily, require explicit signed exception (legal ops). Otherwise, enter FAIL_CLOSED: service returns 503 with residency-evidence bundle for post-incident review.

Telemetry signals to build (minimum viable):
- pin_binding_status (per-tenant): BOUND | UNBOUND | PENDING_MIGRATION
- pin_violation_count (per-hour): increments when a request is routed outside pin_regions while pin_level=HARD
- fallback_route_rate (5m/1h): fraction of requests that hit allowed fallback routes when pin_level=SOFT
- audit_evidence_ids: list of log ids to package for a compliance request (retain per audit_window_days)
- routing_decision_trace (sampled): reason code for routing (capacity, latency, policy, forced)

Suggested alerting thresholds (starter):
- pin_violation_count > 0 for HARD pins -> immediate P1 alert to residency-oncall + acct team
- fallback_route_rate > 2% over 1h for SOFT with SLA <99.9% -> P2
- audit_logging_disabled flag -> P1 (must never happen for pinned tenants)

Operator acceptance test (AAT) checklist (minimal):
- Create pinned tenant with test credentials in target region
- Inject synthetic traffic sequence including KV-cache priming, long context sequences, and streaming completions
- Verify all requests show routing_decision_trace=LOCAL and audit logs include region annotation
- Simulate node failure and confirm behavior matches fallback_policy (for SOFT allow fallback, for HARD fail closed)
- Generate audit evidence bundle and validate format (timestamps, server ids, signed checksums)

Audit evidence packaging (format guidance):
- Bundle = {tenant_id, timeframe, routing_logs (gzip), server_manifest (region ids + instance ids), signed_hash.txt}
- Keep human-friendly cover sheet: what was requested, contract clause pointer, operator who exported bundle. (we'll provide template for sales/legal)

Edge cases and unresolved questions (action items):
- Q1: How to represent dual-legal-jurisdiction customers that require data residency for stored artifacts but allow inference compute in a separate region? (proposal: SALTED pin with explicit fields for storage_regions and compute_regions) — assign to Priya to draft contract language.
- Q2: Telemetry retention vs legal hold — do we create separate retention streams for audit evidence? (legal needs input).
- Q3: Is FAIL_CLOSED acceptable for onboarding customers with <3 months runway? need sales input on conversion risk.

Open TODOs (short):
- [ ] Finalize entitlement field names for API and SOWs (owner: Elena)
- [ ] Add routing_decision_trace sampling to observability pipeline (owner: Oliver)
- [ ] Draft Confluence template for audit evidence bundle (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Run tabletop with SRE and Legal on hard-pin outage scenarios (owner: Priya)

Communication and UX notes for Sales/CS:
- Provide simple 1-page tradeoff sheet for customers: Hard vs Soft vs Salted pins — include implications for cost, downtime, and SLA.
- Sales must tag deals that include pin entitlements so infra planning can reserve capacity earlier (suggest workflow: add Jira RES-PLANNING ticket automatically on deal won).

References and useful links:
- Confluence: region-pin-onramp (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: RES-312 (pinning entitlement model)
- Slack channel: #residency-ops for runbook coordination

Notes to self / working thoughts (informal):
- We should keep default contract to SOFT with opt-in HARD to limit operational surprises.
- Consider productizing a "pinning add-on" for Dedicated where customers can buy reserved pool capacity by region (makes ops easier).
- Need cost model to surface to Sales: incremental monthly cost per reserved vGPU in-region vs using shared pooled capacity.

Last reviewed: Elena Park 2025-02-02.

If you're reading this and want to iterate: please add comments inline in Confluence or ping me in slack. This doc will become the seed for the official playbook and contract templates.
